title: Average complexity is bounded by average cost
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite alphabet, let $\alpha$ be an output type, let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $g:(\mathrm{Fin}\,n\to\Omega)\to\alpha$, and let $\pi$ be a probability distribution on $\Omega$. For any zero-error randomized decision tree computing $g$, the infimum of the average costs over all such trees is at most the average cost of that tree under independent inputs drawn from $\pi$.
hypotheses_covered: $\alpha$ is an output type and $n$ is a nonnegative integer
$T$ is a zero-error randomized decision tree computing $g
